reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Insurer issuance of paper or electronic cards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1986 S.B. 424 ... A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; Effective 1-01-17). Requires each insurer issuing complying motor vehicle liability policies under listed Chapter 303 sections, or its agent, to furnish an insurance identification card to the named insured for each insured vehicle in paper or acceptable electronic format (including cell phone or portable electronic device display).

headings.title: Required information on insurance identification cards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)–(6) and source notes (Effective 1-01-17). Specifies six required card items: insurer name and address, named insured, policy number, policy effective dates, vehicle description (year/make, at least five VIN digits, or 'Fleet' for five or more vehicles), and prominent carry-and-produce statement.

headings.title: New and replacement insurance identification cards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (Effective 1-01-17). Requires issuance of a new card when the insured vehicle changes, an additional vehicle is insured, or a new policy number is assigned, and a replacement card upon the insured's request if the original is lost.

headings.title: Self-insurer identification cards and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and source notes (Effective 1-01-17). Directs the director to furnish self-insurers under § 303.220 an insurance identification card for each self-insured vehicle displaying the self-insurer's name, the word 'self-insured', and the prominent carry-and-produce statement.

headings.title: Carrying, exhibiting, substitute proofs, and mobile-device rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (Effective 1-01-17). Requires carrying the card at all times and exhibiting it on demand to peace officers, commercial vehicle enforcement officers, or commercial vehicle inspectors during lawful stops or accident investigations; mandates § 303.025 citation for failure to exhibit; allows substitute proofs (policy, binder, receipt, photocopy, or mobile image with subsection 2 info); clarifies electronic display is not consent to access other device contents; defines 'mobile electronic device'; and assigns device damage liability to the presenter except for willful or malicious officer/inspector damage.

headings.title: Penalties for fraudulent cards and electronic images
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes (Effective 1-01-17). Makes knowingly or intentionally producing, manufacturing, selling, or distributing a fraudulent insurance card document, photocopy, or mobile electronic image a class E felony, and knowingly or intentionally possessing a fraudulent document/photocopy or using a fraudulent mobile image a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections including subdivisions 2(1)–(6) and 4(1)–(3) and source notes (Effective 1-01-17) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed paper/electronic card rules, self-insurer cards under § 303.220, substitute proofs/non-consent/device-damage liability rules in 5, and felony/misdemeanor fraud distinctions in 6; retained all six draft titles.

headings.title: Financial responsibility duty, storage exception, and enforcement limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1986 S.B. 424 ... A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168; Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039). Prohibits resident owners, nonresidents, and knowing operators of another's uninsured vehicle from operating or registering without required financial responsibility; exempts inoperable or stored vehicles not in operation; directs voluntary registration-suspension and reinstatement rulemaking; makes operating during claimed storage/inoperability a class B misdemeanor (and possible additional subsection violation); limits DOR enforcement unless operated or applied for in violation or registration maintained in violation on two occasions thirty days apart; and grants director rulemaking authority.

headings.title: Acceptable methods of maintaining financial responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039). Requires resident motor vehicle owners to maintain financial responsibility under § 303.160 or a complying motor vehicle liability policy, and requires nonresident owners to maintain financial responsibility conforming to their state of residence.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties, compliance defense, and court sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)–(4) and source notes (Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039). Sets misdemeanor penalties (class D misdemeanor for first violation except as otherwise provided; up to 15 days county jail and $200–$500 fine for subsequent violations with priors pleaded/proven under § 558.021), provides a defense for proving compliance at citation time, and requires court notice to the director plus one of four sanctions: license suspension (§ 303.042(2) duration, 10-day forwarding), four points, § 302.303 supervision order (max once per 36 months) with MSHP/DOR reporting, or nonresident suspension and home-state notice (§§ 303.030, 303.080).

headings.title: Preserved regulatory approval of policy exclusions and limitations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039). Clarifies that listed Chapter 303 sections do not prohibit the Department of Commerce and Insurance from approving or authorizing exclusions and limitations in automobile liability and uninsured motorist policies.

headings.title: Direct Chapter 512 appeal of court-ordered suspension
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039). Allows an offender to appeal a court-ordered suspension directly under Chapter 512 and specifies that § 302.311 does not apply.

headings.title: Installment payment plans for fines owed to state
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes (Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039). Makes fines owed to the state under this section eligible for installment payment and directs the director to promulgate payment-plan rules accounting for individuals' ability to pay.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections including subdivisions 3(1)–(4) and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168; Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed resident/nonresident/knowing-operator duties, inoperable/stored vehicle exception and voluntary suspension, DOR enforcement triggers, § 558.021 prior pleading and compliance-at-citation defense, Commerce & Insurance exclusion approval, Chapter 512 appeal, and installment plans; retained all six draft titles.

headings.title: Director notices to registering motor vehicle owners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(5) and source notes (L. 1986 S.B. 424 ... A.L. 2020 H.B. 1963; cross-references re § 226.008 agency transfers). Requires the director to inform registering owners of the financial responsibility mandate, proof-at-registration requirement (in bold colored print at least 30 days before renewal month), violation penalties, benefits of excess coverage, and compliance sampling authority.

headings.title: Registration affidavit, proof of insurance, and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (including cross-references noting that the Division of Motor Carrier and Railroad Safety and Highway Reciprocity Commission were abolished and transferred under § 226.008). Requires a signed, processor-acknowledged (unnotarized) affidavit bearing a bold § 575.050 false-affidavit warning plus § 303.024 card or prescribed proof at registration, with exceptions for §§ 301.271–301.279 reciprocity registrations and § 390.126 motor-carrier-insured vehicles.

headings.title: Compliance sampling and insurer electronic policy reporting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and source notes. Authorizes the director to use compliance sampling techniques and verify financial responsibility, and (beginning January 1, 2001) to require electronic reporting from insurers of private passenger noncommercial policy issuance, nonrenewal, cancellation, termination, or revocation (excluding fleet, rental, and commercial line policies) for sampling.

headings.title: Ownership, confidentiality, and limited disclosure of insurer data
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1)–(7) and source notes. Designates insurer-provided data as insurer property exempt from Chapter 610 disclosure, permits DOR enforcement use, and restricts coverage-status disclosure exclusively to seven enumerated requesters (individual, minor's parent/guardian, incapacitated person's guardian, power-of-attorney holder, 90-day notarized-release holder, accident claimant, and state auditor).

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and Chapter 536 nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Grants director rulemaking authority for subsection 3(1)–(3), subjects rules to Chapter 536 and § 536.028, and includes a nonseverability clause rendering the rulemaking grant and post-August 28, 2000 rules void if legislative rule-review powers under Chapter 536 are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Unauthorized disclosure penalty and insurer immunity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes. Makes knowing unauthorized disclosure of insurer-provided data a class A misdemeanor and immunizes insurers from civil liability for performing section duties except for willful and wanton acts of omission.

headings.title: Administrative penalties for insurer noncompliance and excuse
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes. Requires DOR to notify the Department of Commerce and Insurance of insurer violations, authorizes up to $500 per day administrative penalties for knowing noncompliance (excusable for inadvertent, accidental, or excusable neglect), and sets an effective date six months after CSR rule publication.

headings.title: Verification notice to owner or operator and suspension
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes. Requires the director to notify an owner or operator to provide proof of financial responsibility within fifteen days (including insurer, policy number, and expiration date as requested), with vehicle registration and applicable driving-privilege suspension for failure to provide the information.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all eight subsections including subdivisions 1(1)–(5), 3(1)–(3), and 4(1)–(7) and source notes (including both § 226.008 cross-references recording abolition and transfer of the Division of Motor Carrier and Railroad Safety and Highway Reciprocity Commission), and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed § 575.050 affidavit warning, Chapter 610 confidentiality and seven disclosure exceptions, Chapter 536 nonseverability clause, and insurer penalties; retained all eight draft titles.

headings.title: Security determination after accident and burden of proof
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.050 ... A.L. 2018 S.B. 708; Effective 7-01-19; 1997 Tatum v. Van Liner Ins. Co. annotation on UM setoff). Directs the director, within 20 days after receiving an accident report involving injury, death, or over-$500 property damage without satisfactory proof of release, nonliability adjudication, or installment agreement, to determine sufficient security; places the burden of proving lack of fault on any challenger.

headings.title: Suspension for failure to deposit security and notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (Effective 7-01-19). Requires the director within 90 days of an accident report to suspend involved operators' licenses, owners' registrations, and nonresidents' operating or vehicle-use privileges unless determined security is deposited, with at least 10 days' advance notice; specifies suspension is in addition to §§ 303.041 and 303.042 suspensions.

headings.title: Action after receiving corrected insurance or bond information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (Effective 7-01-19). Directs the director to take appropriate action within 45 days after receiving correct information whenever erroneous information was previously given regarding subsection 4(1)–(3) coverage matters.

headings.title: Exemptions under 303.070, insurance, bonds, and self-insurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1)–(4) and source notes (Effective 7-01-19). Excludes § 303.070 conditions and four coverage categories from section application: owner's liability policy, non-owner operator's liability policy or bond, other director-accepted liability policy or bond, and § 303.220 self-insurers and their drivers.

headings.title: Authorized insurers and sureties, exceptions, and minimum limits
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Qualifying insurers, out-of-state carriers, and minimum limits" to explicitly cover both insurance companies and surety companies alongside the out-of-state power-of-attorney exception. Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (Effective 7-01-19; 1997 Tatum v. Van Liner Ins. Co. annotation on statutory minimum UM setoff). Requires qualifying policies or bonds to be issued by Missouri-authorized insurance or surety companies—or unauthorized carriers for out-of-state registered vehicles executing a power of attorney for service of process—with minimum limits of $25,000/$50,000 bodily injury or death and $25,000 property damage.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections including subdivisions 4(1)–(4) and source notes (Effective 7-01-19; 1997 Tatum v. Van Liner Ins. Co. UM setoff annotation) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 5 to "Authorized insurers and sureties, exceptions, and minimum limits" to explicitly include surety companies alongside insurers and the out-of-state POA exception; retained subsections 1–4.

headings.title: Required accident reports, form notices, and incapacity filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and continuation text in subdivision (3), plus history note (L. 1953 p. 569 ... A.L. 2010 S.B. 583). Requires 30-day written accident reports for qualifying uninsured-motorist accidents (death, injury, or over-$500 property damage, including parked cars and public/private lots) or uninsured drivers/owners; specifies three mandatory form notices (claim responsibility, security use, 1-year return/§ 303.060); and in the continuation of (3) covers §§ 303.030/303.025 coverage data, director reliance, owner or delayed operator-owner filing with doctor's certificate upon physical incapacity, and additional requested information.

headings.title: Director notice to other parties and information requests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 ... A.L. 2010 S.B. 583). Requires the director within 10 days of receiving a report to notify all other listed involved parties, who must furnish requested information within 10 days.

headings.title: Reporting accidents involving nonresident uninsured motorists
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 ... A.L. 2010 S.B. 583). Mandates reporting by nonresident uninsured motorists and responding law enforcement agencies, and permits resident operators or owners involved with an uninsured nonresident motorist to report under subsections 1 and 2.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions 1(1)–(3) and the long continuation text embedded inside subdivision 1(3), plus history note (through A.L. 2010 S.B. 583), and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed subsection 1 title covers reporting triggers, form notices, and physical-incapacity filing with doctor's certificate; retained all three draft titles.

headings.title: Suspension notice, effective timing, and hearing stay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1986 S.B. 424 ... A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168; Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039). Directs suspension of driving privilege and/or vehicle registration 33 days after mailing notice (deemed received 3 days after mailing) to the last known address, specifies required notice contents (grounds, effective date, hearing right/procedure/deadline), and stays suspension pending final order if a hearing request is received before the effective date.

headings.title: Later insurance, ownership changes, transfers, and surrender fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039). Provides, except as otherwise provided by law, that post-verification or post-conviction insurance acquisition or ownership termination does not affect suspension; keeps suspensions in force across registration renewals, new registrations, and transfers; and bars extending suspensions for delinquent late surrender fees effective January 1, 2000.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168; Effective 1-01-24, see § 303.039) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed 33-day mailing/3-day deemed receipt timing, hearing stay, post-verification insurance/ownership/transfer rules, and January 1, 2000 late surrender fee bar; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Effective date of suspension after notice receipt
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1986 S.B. 424, A.L. 1999 S.B. 19, A.L. 2000 H.B. 1797; Effective 3-01-01). Sets the suspension effective date at thirty days after deemed receipt of the § 303.041 notice by ordinary mail.

headings.title: Tiered suspension periods, reinstatement fees, and proof
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and source notes (Effective 3-01-01). Establishes tiered suspension durations and reinstatement fees plus proof of insurance (§ 303.026 or prescribed form): no prior violation ($20 fee), one prior within two years (90 days and $200 fee), and two or more priors (one year and $400 fee).

headings.title: Extension for unfiled proof and no period reduction
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Extension of suspension for unfiled proof of insurance" to cover both sentences of subsection 3, including the non-reduction rule. Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (Effective 3-01-01). Extends the suspension period if required proof of insurance is not filed before the period ends, and specifies that filing proof never reduces any suspension period.

headings.title: One-year suspension for submitting false proof of insurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (Effective 3-01-01; 2007 Hudson v. Director of Revenue annotation holding strict liability with no knowledge element for false insurance card submission). Requires suspending vehicle registration and driving privilege for false proof of insurance, terminable after one year upon a $150 reinstatement fee and proof of insurance.

headings.title: Limit on high-risk insurance certificates and accident exception
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Limit on requiring high-risk insurance certificates" to preserve the express exclusion for accidents involving an uninsured party. Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (Effective 3-01-01). Prohibits the director from requiring a § 303.170 or § 303.180 insurance certificate or other high-risk insurance to terminate a suspension under this section, excluding motor vehicle accident cases where one or more parties were uninsured.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections including subdivisions 2(1)–(3) and source notes (Effective 3-01-01; 2007 Hudson v. Director of Revenue strict-liability annotation for false proof in subsection 4), and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 3 to "Extension for unfiled proof and no period reduction" and subsection 5 to "Limit on high-risk insurance certificates and accident exception" to preserve the uninsured-accident carve-out; retained subsections 1, 2, and 4.

headings.title: Security form, maximum limits, and covered-person specification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.090, A.L. 1986 S.B. 424; Effective 7-01-87). Authorizes the director to set security form and amount up to § 303.030 limits, requires written specification of covered persons, and allows written amendment to add covered persons required to furnish security from the same accident.

headings.title: Reducing excessive security and returning excess deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (Effective 7-01-87). Permits the director within one year to reduce excessive security orders and mandates immediate return of any excess deposited amount to the depositor or personal representative notwithstanding § 303.060.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (Effective 7-01-87) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed § 303.030 security cap, same-accident written covered-person specification/amendment in 1, and one-year excessive-security reduction/return notwithstanding § 303.060 in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Deposit with director and permitted judgment or settlement uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.100, A.L. 1957 p. 634, A.L. 1986 S.B. 424; Effective 7-01-87). Requires security deposits to be held by the director of revenue solely to pay judgments in actions filed within one year of the accident (or within one year of a § 303.140(3) deposit) or depositor-agreed claim settlements.

headings.title: Conditions for returning security deposits or balances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (Effective 7-01-87). Directs return of the deposit or balance to the depositor, personal representative, or assignee upon satisfactory evidence of release, final nonliability adjudication, a § 303.070(3) agreement, or after one year upon reasonable evidence of no pending action or unpaid judgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (Effective 7-01-87) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed one-year action/§ 303.140(3) and settlement payout scope in 1 and § 303.070(3)/one-year return conditions in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Compliance prerequisite for unlicensed, unregistered, or nonresident persons
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Compliance prerequisite for unlicensed drivers and nonresidents" to include unregistered owners as well as unlicensed operators and nonresidents. Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569). Bars unlicensed or unregistered accident participants and nonresidents from obtaining a Missouri license or registration until complying with Chapter 303 to the same extent as if previously licensed and registered.

headings.title: Reciprocal notice of nonresident operating privilege suspensions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569). Directs the director to transmit a certified copy of a § 303.030 or § 303.140 nonresident operating-privilege suspension to the nonresident's home-state licensing official if that state has similar reciprocal law under subsection 3.

headings.title: Reciprocal suspension of residents after out-of-state action
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569). Requires the director, upon out-of-state certification of a resident's suspension or revocation for failing to deposit accident security under comparable circumstances, to suspend the resident's license and registrations until compliance with the other state's security law is shown.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1953 p. 569) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 to "Compliance prerequisite for unlicensed, unregistered, or nonresident persons" to include unregistered owners; retained reciprocal notice and suspension titles for subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: Court forwarding of unsatisfied final judgments after sixty days
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.120). Requires the court clerk, or judge where there is no clerk, to forward a certified copy of a qualifying final judgment to the director immediately after sixty days of nonpayment.

headings.title: Transmitting unsatisfied nonresident judgments to home state
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.120). Requires the director to immediately transmit a certified copy of any reported judgment against a nonresident defendant to the licensing and registration official of the defendant's state of residence.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.120) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed 60-day court forwarding (clerk or judge) in 1 and immediate nonresident transmission to home state in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Immediate suspension on certified judgment and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Immediate suspension upon receiving certified unsatisfied judgment" to preserve the express exceptions under this section and § 303.130. Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.130). Requires the director upon receiving a certified copy of a judgment to immediately suspend the debtor's license, registration, and nonresident operating privilege, except as otherwise provided in this section and § 303.130.

headings.title: Discretionary allowance with creditor consent and proof
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Discretionary license allowance with judgment-creditor written consent" to cover license, registration, and nonresident operating privilege and include the required proof of financial responsibility. Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.130). Authorizes the director, in his discretion, to allow license, registration, or nonresident privilege for six months and until written revocation upon the judgment-creditor's written consent and the debtor's proof of financial responsibility, despite default on the judgment or § 303.130 installments.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.130) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 to "Immediate suspension on certified judgment and exceptions" (preserving section/§ 303.130 exceptions) and subsection 2 to "Discretionary allowance with creditor consent and proof" (covering license, registration, and nonresident privilege plus proof of financial responsibility).

headings.title: Payment thresholds deeming judgments satisfied under chapter
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and source notes (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.150 ... A.L. 2018 S.B. 708; Effective 7-01-19). Sets dollar credit thresholds deeming judgments satisfied for Chapter 303 purposes only: $25,000 for injury or death of one person, $50,000 for two or more persons, and $25,000 for property damage from one accident.

headings.title: Crediting settlement payments toward satisfaction amounts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (Effective 7-01-19). Requires payments made in settlement of motor vehicle accident injury, death, or property-damage claims to be credited in reduction of subsection 1 amounts.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)–(3) and source notes (Effective 7-01-19) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed Chapter 303-only satisfaction thresholds ($25k/$50k/$25k) in 1 and settlement credit reduction in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Court order permitting installment payment of judgment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.160). Permits a judgment-debtor, on due notice to the creditor, to apply to the rendering court for a discretionary order fixing installment payments without prejudice to the creditor's other legal remedies.

headings.title: Withholding or restoring privileges during compliant installments
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Withholding or restoring license during compliant installments" to cover license, registration, and nonresident operating privilege rather than license alone. Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.160). Bars suspension and requires restoration of a suspended license, registration, or nonresident privilege when the judgment-debtor furnishes proof of financial responsibility, obtains an installment order, and is not in default.

headings.title: Immediate suspension upon installment payment default
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.160). Directs the director, upon notice of default on any court-ordered installment, to immediately suspend the debtor's license, registration, or nonresident operating privilege until the judgment is satisfied under Chapter 303.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.160) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 to "Withholding or restoring privileges during compliant installments" so registrations and nonresident operating privileges are not narrowed to licenses; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Registration suspension on conviction or forfeiture and exception
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Registration suspension upon conviction or bail forfeiture" to preserve the proof-of-financial-responsibility exception. Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.170). Requires suspending all motor vehicle registrations whenever the director suspends or revokes a license upon conviction or bail forfeiture, unless proof of financial responsibility is previously or immediately given and maintained (and unless otherwise required by law).

headings.title: Continued suspension until proof of financial responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.170). Continues license and registration suspension or revocation and bars renewal, new license issuance, or vehicle registration until permitted under motor vehicle laws and until proof of financial responsibility is given and maintained.

headings.title: Licensing and registration bar for unlicensed offenders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.170). Bars issuing a license or continuing or granting vehicle registration for an unlicensed person convicted of or forfeiting bail/collateral on a suspension/revocation offense, unlicensed driving, or unregistered vehicle operation until proof of financial responsibility is given and maintained.

headings.title: Continued suspension of nonresident operating privileges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.170). Continues suspension or revocation of a nonresident's operating privilege imposed for conviction or bail forfeiture unless proof of financial responsibility was previously or is immediately given and maintained.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.170) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 to "Registration suspension on conviction or forfeiture and exception" to preserve the proof-of-responsibility carve-out; retained subsections 2, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Authorized methods for filing proof of financial responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(4) and source notes (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.180, A.L. 1961 p. 463; 1974 American Family Ins. Co. v. Missouri Power and Light Co. annotation noting a self-insurance certificate is not an insurance policy). headings.title: Vehicle registration conditioned on furnishing required proof
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Prohibits registering or continuing registration of a motor vehicle in the name of any person required to file proof of financial responsibility unless proof is furnished for that vehicle.

headings.title: Filing authorized insurer certificates and vehicle designation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.190). Allows furnishing proof of financial responsibility via a Missouri-authorized insurer's written certificate stating the matching policy effective date and explicitly describing or referencing covered vehicles (unless issued to a non-owner).

headings.title: Registration limited to vehicles designated in certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.190). Prohibits registering or continuing registration of a motor vehicle for a person required to file proof unless the vehicle is designated in such an insurance certificate.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.190) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed non-owner exception in vehicle designation (1) and registration restriction to designated vehicles (2); retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Nonresident insurance certificates and carrier compliance conditions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(2) and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.200). Allows a nonresident owner (or non-owner) to furnish proof through a certificate from a carrier authorized in the vehicle's registration state (or insured's residence state), conditioned on the carrier executing a power of attorney for service of process and agreeing in writing that policies conform to Missouri law.

headings.title: Disqualification of defaulting unauthorized insurance carriers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.200). Bars the director from accepting past or tendered certificates from an unauthorized insurance carrier while it remains in default on its undertakings or agreements under subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)–(2) and history note (L. 1953 p. 569 § 303.200) and verified source identity and fingerprints. headings.title: Creation, custody, and dedicated use of enforcement fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398). Creates the Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Verification and Enforcement Fund in the state treasury for DOR receipts under §§ 303.420–303.440, names the state treasurer custodian with disbursement authority under §§ 30.170 and 30.180, and dedicates moneys solely to DOR administration of §§ 303.420–303.440.

headings.title: Exemption from biennial general revenue reversion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398). Exempts remaining fund moneys at the end of a biennium from reverting to the general revenue fund notwithstanding § 33.080.

headings.title: Investment of fund moneys and credited earnings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398). Directs the state treasurer to invest fund moneys like other state funds and credit all earned interest and moneys to the fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed §§ 30.170/30.180 disbursement and §§ 303.420–303.440 dedicated use (1), § 33.080 non-reversion (2), and investment/credited earnings (3); retained all three draft titles.

headings.title: Program creation, vendor contracts, diversion, and automated-system ban
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(4) and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Creates the DOR enforcement and compliance incentive program, authorizes third-party vendor contracts, directs technological comparison of registration and financial responsibility data with optional pretrial diversion, prohibits use of automated camera/sensor enforcement systems (defined in (3)), and allows funding vendor fees from pretrial diversion fees.

headings.title: Authorized technology data collection for enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Authorizes DOR to permit law enforcement agencies or third-party vendors to use technology to collect data for investigating, detecting, analyzing, and enforcing motor vehicle financial responsibility law.

headings.title: Authorized administration of notices, fees, and referrals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Authorizes DOR to permit traffic enforcement officers or third-party vendors to process and issue violation notices, collect violation fees, or refer cases for prosecution under the program.

headings.title: Restricted system access and vendor maintenance collaboration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Restricts verification system access to qualified agencies and contracted third-party vendors, while permitting contracted technology/equipment/maintenance vendors to collaborate as necessary for software updates and maintenance.

headings.title: Matched insurance and registration data as violation evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Permits collected data matched to system-verified insurance records and Missouri vehicle registration databases to identify violations and deems such corresponding data evidence of violations.

headings.title: Registration suspension under 303.041 for program violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Directs DOR, except as otherwise provided in this section, to suspend vehicle registrations in accordance with § 303.041 when determined under the program to be in violation of financial responsibility law.

headings.title: Violation notices, pretrial diversion, hearings, referrals, and reinstatement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Establishes full enforcement workflow: 30-day initial notice (proof or pending criminal charge response and website info), 33-day suspension notice (grounds, hearing rights, $300 minimum penalty/prosecution warning, and diversion offer), pretrial diversion terms (up to $200 fee, 2-year maintenance, no § 302.302 points, suspension/prosecution for noncompliance), hearing stay except as to diversion eligibility, mailing/receipts/§ 303.422 fund deposits, and reinstatement upon proof and § 303.042(2)-equivalent nonrefundable fee.

headings.title: Data use limits, evidence, and probable cause affidavits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Restricts program data to financial responsibility enforcement, designates law enforcement data as evidence upon confirmed noncompliance, and states that such evidence plus an identifying affidavit constitutes probable cause forwarded to the prosecuting attorney under subsection 7.

headings.title: Non-appearance dispute options, compliance dismissal, and system recording
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Requires dispute options without court or administrative appearance, entitles owners providing timely proof of compliance at the alleged violation time to dismissal without fees or fines, and directs recording compliance proof in the § 303.430 system.

headings.title: Prohibition on bias in program data collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Requires program data collection to be conducted in a manner prohibiting bias toward any specific community, race, gender, or socioeconomic status.

headings.title: Data sale and sharing bans and breach liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Prohibits law enforcement agencies, vendors, or other authorized entities from selling program data or sharing it for unauthorized purposes, requires securing all data, and states that vendors or other authorized entities may be liable for data security breaches.

headings.title: Exclusion of fleet and commercial auto vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Prohibits DOR from taking action under §§ 303.420–303.440 against § 301.032 fleet vehicles or vehicles known to DOR to be insured under commercial auto coverage as defined in § 303.430(2)(10).

headings.title: Five-year annual legislative reports and government data rules
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Five-year annual legislative reports and local data rules" because rulemaking covers information from the state as well as counties and municipalities. Read complete text of subsection 13 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Requires annual DOR reports to specified legislative leaders and committees for five years starting one year after implementation (covering operations, costs, effectiveness, and anonymized race and zip-code demographics), and authorizes rules requiring state, county, and municipal data for the report.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and Chapter 536 nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Grants DOR rulemaking authority subject to Chapter 536 and § 536.028 and includes a nonseverability clause rendering the rulemaking grant and post-August 28, 2023 rules void if legislative rule-review powers under Chapter 536 are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Web-based verification system establishment and superseding scope
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Directs DOR to establish and maintain a web-based financial responsibility verification system, provide data access, and require insurer functionality under §§ 303.420–303.440, superseding existing systems as the sole Chapter 303 verification system subject to statutory and implementation-guide exceptions.

headings.title: System standards, advisory council, insurer duties, and exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)–(13) and (4)(a)–(i) and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Sets comprehensive system rules: IICMVA web services, security, 12-month DOR retention cap, NAIC/VIN matching, small-insurer (1,000 or fewer vehicles) and non-policy alternatives, out-of-state exclusion; response times and downtime/outage safe harbors; non-effect on individual claim investigations and DOR vendor contracts; 1-year advisory council and voting membership; implementation guide and contact persons; targeted requests, P&C insurer compliance, and 6-month insurer records; commercial auto coverage definition, exemption, voluntary participation, and commercial/fleet ID cards; insurer good-faith civil/administrative immunity; and insurer third-party vendor use.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and Chapter 536 nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 398, A.L. 2024 S.B. 1359). Directs DOR to promulgate rules for §§ 303.420–303.440 subject to Chapter 536 and § 536.028 and includes a nonseverability clause rendering the rulemaking grant and post-August 28, 2023 rules void if legislative rule-review powers under Chapter 536 are held unconstitutional.
